title: Console: Reconcile scope for slimmed dashboard + tracing + cost-breakdown MVP
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Follow-up to PRD v2.0: reconcile feature scope for the Console observability MVP given execution constraints (telemetry readiness, infra bandwidth, and design availability). This ticket captures explicit cuts and the acceptance criteria for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown so engineering and design have a single source of truth for the planned MVP slice.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: Launch with 3 aggregated cards (p95 latency by model, token cost per 10k tokens, error rate %); each card links to a lightweight per-route table view (no time-series zoom or per-token drilldown)

Tracing: Provide sampled traces for 'model_infer' and 'route_handler' with top-5 latency spans; capture basic span attributes (timestamp, span_name, duration, trace_id) and a link to raw logs. No long-trace visualization or flamegraph in MVP.
Cost breakdown: Show per-route token vs infra split for the last 24h and last 7d with simple percentage bars; exclude per-user, per-api-key, and prediction-level attribution in MVP.
Rollout: Feature flags in place (console.observability.dashboards, .tracing, .cost_breakdown) and gated rollout to internal beta orgs before 25% of external customers.
Telemetry: Ingestion backlog is under threshold and retention for crude telemetry is available for 7 days for MVP metrics and 30 days for cost aggregates.
Docs: Short-form console help + one-page runbook for on-call with known limitations and fallback steps.
QA: End-to-end smoke tests for each card and tracing link; perf benchmark shows dashboard page load < 1.5s for internal test org with realistic token load.
notes: Design pushed alternate mocks for a single-pane timeline but will not be implemented in MVP due to frontend rendering cost.
Engineering requested to drop session-level trace correlation and complex KV cache visualizations — accepted to meet ship date.
PM prioritized customer-visible metrics that reduce support toil (latency, cost, errors) over deep diagnostic tooling in initial launch.
Follow-on work to reintroduce per-user cost and flamegraphs is tracked under PM-16200 and ENG-19821.
Security: KMS access for cost data confirmed with infra; no additional PII in MVP metrics.
decisions: Cut: Remove time-series zoom and per-token drilldowns from dashboard MVP to reduce query complexity.
Cut: No full-trace flamegraphs or waterfall visualizations for MVP; only sampled traces with top spans.
Keep: Per-route summary cards that provide the highest signal-to-noise for customer support and cost decisions.
Defer: Per-api-key billing breakdown and export CSV functionality to post-MVP.
